citation: Schwaab et al. (2021), The role of urban trees in reducing land surface temperatures in European cities
source_family: European multi-city Landsat and land-cover analysis
supports: tree-covered areas can have lower LST than urban fabric within the studied European cities
cooling magnitude varies with climate and water availability
limitations: isolated street trees may be underrepresented

citation: Ettinger et al. (2024), Tree canopy cover and summertime air temperature in South Tacoma
source_family: South Tacoma summer sidewalk sensor study
supports: within this local study, higher nearby canopy was associated with lower summertime air temperature
threshold probabilities differed by canopy cover
does_not_support: full human heat exposure or health effect
limitations: temperature rather than humidity or full heat index

citation: Ralls et al. (2024), Urban tree canopy and near-surface air temperature in Portland, Oregon
supports: air temperature decreased with canopy and increased with imperviousness within the Portland study
does_not_support: generalization to all cities or all times
limitations: repository record used for detailed metadata

citation: Ziter et al. (2019), Scale-dependent interactions between tree canopy cover and impervious surfaces reduce daytime urban heat during summer
source_family: Madison mobile air-temperature and land-cover study
supports: canopy and imperviousness interact at spatial scales in the Madison study
limitations: nighttime and microclimate interpretation requires care

citation: Wujeska-Klause and Pfautsch (2020), The Best Urban Trees for Daytime Cooling Leave Nights Slightly Warmer
source_family: Sydney street-level tree day/night boundary study
supports: daytime cooling can coexist with slightly warmer nights under dense canopies
radiation and ventilation are relevant mechanisms
does_not_support: all species or urban forms behaving alike

citation: Meili et al. (2021), Vegetation cooling in cities depends on photosynthetic pathway and atmospheric conditions
supports: transpiration and roughness can cool under some conditions
non-transpiring vegetation can warm local air in some hours in the model
climate and atmospheric conditions modify the direction and size
limitations: mechanistic model rather than direct causal observation

citation: McDonald et al. (2021), The tree cover and temperature disparity in US urbanized areas
source_family: US national tree-cover and summer Landsat disparity analysis
supports: tree cover and heat disparities co-locate in the studied US urbanized areas
the pattern persists after reported covariate controls
does_not_support: near-surface air or human heat equivalence

citation: World Meteorological Organization (2023), State of the Climate in Europe and urban climate guidance material, WMO-No. 1292
supports: urban heat is context-dependent and requires careful measurement and adaptation framing
does_not_support: a universal canopy causal estimate from this document alone
limitations: PDF text extraction was limited in this run
synthesis and guidance rather than one original effect study
specific canopy claim requires source-level inspection

citation: CDC Field Epidemiology Manual, Analyze and Interpret Data
supports: association and statistical significance alone do not establish causation
confounding, selection, information error, timing, and effect modification must be assessed
does_not_support: causal promotion of the replay findings
limitations: guidance rather than a canopy study
does not resolve the substantive urban-climate effect
